subject: Converting the negative binomial model script to Poisson log normal model script

messages.author: d6a22ac7ce11aa1b
messages.subject: Converting the negative binomial model script to Poisson log normal model script
parts:
Hi All,

I am currently working on count data, where I fitted them using negative binomial model (see the attached script). Is it possible I can convert the same script to Poisson log normal model? 

Because I would also like to compare the model fit using the DIC value.

Thanks
### specifying the poisson-gamma model
negbin<-"
data{
int<lower=0> N;                           # rows of data
vector[N] studyperiod;
vector[N] majaadt;
vector[N] minaadt;                    # predictor variable
vector[N] majlane;
vector[N] minlane;
vector[N] medianwidth;
vector[N] speed;
vector[N] landuse;
vector[N] mediantype;
int<lower=0> totalcrashes[N];            # response variable
}

parameters {
real<lower=0> phi;      # negative binomial dispersion parameter
real beta0;             # intercept
real beta3;
real beta5;
real beta6;
real beta7;
real beta8;
real beta9;
real beta10;
real beta11;
real beta12;
}

model {
### priors
phi ~    cauchy (0.001,0.001);
beta0 ~ normal(0.0,1E4);
beta3 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta5 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta6 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta7 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta8 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta9 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta10 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta11 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta12 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
# data model
totalcrashes ~ neg_binomial_2_log(beta0 + beta3*studyperiod + beta5*majaadt + beta6*minaadt + beta7*majlane + beta8*minlane + beta9*speed + beta10*landuse + beta11*medianwidth + beta12*mediantype, phi);
}
"

write(negbin, file="negbin-glm-CB.stan")
CB<-stan_model("negbin-glm-CB.stan")
set.seed(1000)
N<- 276
phi<-  0.524658  
beta0<- -3.279956
beta3<- -0.0709271 
beta5<-  0.0807461
beta6<-   0.3647194
beta7<- 0.0069352
beta8<- 0.0548912
beta9<-  0.7149454
beta10<- 0.3034317 
beta11<-  0.0014502 
beta12<- -0.1764844
comparisonbefore<-sampling(CB, data=list(N=N, totalcrashes=crashdata_CB$totalcrashes, studyperiod=crashdata_CB$studyperiod, majaadt=crashdata_CB$majaadt, minaadt=crashdata_CB$minaadt, majlane=crashdata_CB$majlane, minlane=crashdata_CB$minlane, speed=crashdata_CB$speed, landuse=crashdata_CB$landuse, medianwidth=crashdata_CB$medianwidth, mediantype=crashdata_CB$mediantype), 
                          pars=c("beta0", "beta3", "beta5", "beta6", "beta7", "beta8", "beta9", "beta10", "beta11", "beta12",  "phi"),
                          iter=5000, warmup=1000, chains=4)

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Re: Converting the negative binomial model script to Poisson log normal model script
parts:
Sure, just omit phi and use poisson_log( ... ) instead.

BTW, you sd on the normal's are huge. I would change them to normal(0, 5), especially
regarding to your results which are not in the 10e4 range. 

Andre

messages.author: 71c315ee557ff234
messages.subject: Re: Converting the negative binomial model script to Poisson log normal model script
parts:
The poisson_log only takes no phi parameter. 

remove those lines;
real<lower=0> phi;      # negative binomial dispersion parameter

phi ~    cauchy (0.001,0.001);


replace by:

totalcrashes ~ neg_binomial_2_log(beta0 + beta3*studyperiod + beta5*majaadt + beta6*minaadt + beta7*majlane + beta8*minlane + beta9*speed + beta10*landuse + beta11*medianwidth + beta12*mediantype, phi);

with:

totalcrashes ~ poisson_log(beta0 + beta3*studyperiod + beta5*majaadt + beta6*minaadt + beta7*majlane + beta8*minlane + beta9*speed + beta10*landuse + beta11*medianwidth + beta12*mediantype);

and everywhere else you see a phi.
Take a look at stan_glm which is easier as I see there are no special a-prior hyperparameters. 

Andre

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Converting the negative binomial model script to Poisson log normal model script
parts:
You probably also don't want cauchy(0.001, 0.001).

That puts most of the mass in a very narrow range but
leaves a fat tail.

You're having problems trying to define a variable named
after one of our built-in functions, poisson_log. Just
choose a different name for a local variable.

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Converting the negative binomial model script to Poisson log normal model script
parts:
On a different note, you say you want to compare on DIC. We don't recommend DIC (or WAIC really) for various reasons described in our paper
Practical Bayesian Model Evaluation Using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation and WAIC. An open access preprint is available on arxiv here

https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.04544

and the version accepted for publication is here

http://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2Fs11222-016-9696-4

Hope that helps and feel free to follow up if you have any questions about applying the approach in the paper to your models.

Jonah

Hi All,

Thank you for technical responses. All of them are very useful.

I still have issue with the poisson lognormal model. I was able to get the results with the poisson_log function, but I would also like to incorporate the extra variation term (as the overdispersion parameter).

I will appreciate any ideas please on how I can implement that parameter.

y_(i,t)  ~ Poisson(ε_i λ_(i,t)) 
Where:
y_(i,t) =    Observed number of crashes at site i in year t
λ_(i,t) =    Expected number of crashes at intersection I in year t
ε_i =    Multiplicative random effect at site i
The main difference between the Poisson-Lognormal and Poisson-Gamma model in estimating the expected crashes is on estimating the multiplicative random effect for site i. the following equations describe the estimation of ε_i for the two models.
For the Poisson-Lognormal model, ε_i  ~ LogN(0,σ^2)
For the Poisson-Gamma model, ε_i  ~ Gamma(φ,(1/φ)
